answer: Fork-divergence audit: each agent carries a line of signed, hash-chained state roots. A challenger picks a random past block, tasks the agent with a sparrow-path replay to that point, and checks the root against the published canyon of history. Clones share every root, so passing proves nothing; catching one agent diverging from its line reveals the fork and flags its whole twin set in one tide of invalidations. Cost: attackers must clone perfectly and never let any copy drift, so one accidental desync or partial update sinks every sybil at once.
